chunks: 1- Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid from Uthman ibn Isa from Sama'ah ibn Mihran from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who is found dead in a village or between two villages, so he said: The distance between them is measured, and whichever is closer, its people are liable (for the blood money).
2- Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), like it.

3- Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran from Asim ibn Humayd from Muhammad ibn Qays who said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled in the case of a man killed in a village or near a village that the people of that village are liable (for blood money) if no evidence is produced against the people of that village that they killed him. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: The meaning in these narrations is that the people of the village or tribe are only liable if the dead man is found among them, provided they are suspected of killing him and refuse to take the oath, as we have explained in our Great Book. As for if they are not suspected of killing him or if they respond to the oath, then there is no blood money upon them, and his blood money is paid from the treasury (Bayt al-Mal), and that which indicates this.
4- What Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad and al-Abbas and al-Haytham all from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn al-Fudayl from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When a man is found killed in the tribe of a people, they are all sworn an oath that they did not kill him and do not know his killer. If they refuse, they pay the blood money among themselves from their wealth, equally among all the tribe from the adult men.
5- From him (Muhammad ibn Qays) from Harun ibn Muslim from Mas'adah ibn Ziyad from Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said: My father (peace be upon him) was...

If the people do not produce evidence for killing their dead man and do not swear that the suspects killed him, he swears the suspects fifty oaths by God that they did not kill him and did not know his killer. Then the blood money is paid to the heirs of the dead man, and that is if he was killed in one tribe. As for if he was killed in a camp or a market or a city, his blood money is paid to his heirs from the treasury.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling for blood money when a body is found in a village and the killer is unknown?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Istibsar elucidates the jurisprudence of *diyah* for an unknown killer (*qatil ghayr ma'lum*) found in a specific locality, emphasizing the Shia principle of collective liability (*ta'abbut*) contingent upon suspicion and the refusal to swear oaths. Imam al-Sadiq and Imam al-Baqir clarify that while residents of villages or tribes bear the cost if they withhold oaths, those in larger public spaces like markets or cities have their *diyah* paid from the state treasury (*Bayt al-Mal*), reflecting the administrative distinction between localized kinship responsibility and broader civic governance.
